findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (passed 66 to 47); Cairns recorded Aye
findings.note: House vote on the second reading of the Election Law Changes bill. The ratified text requires a voter registration application to affirmatively state US citizenship before it is processed (with a 30-day notice and sworn-statement fix if the question is left blank) and directs the State Board of Elections to create a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. The ratified text was later vetoed by the Governor per the bill page.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (passed 62 to 47); Cairns recorded Aye
findings.note: House vote to concur with the Senate changes to the Election Law Changes bill, sending it to the Governor; the bill page lists a Governor's veto and a veto-override calendar placement for 09/02/2026.

findings.motion: Co-sponsor of HB 825 Election Improvements (date shown is the bill's introduction date; date she was added not seen)
findings.note: Cairns is listed as a co-sponsor. Filed text bans ranked choice voting, changes election-related activity rules, shortens early voting, and changes the identification rules for requesting an absentee ballot: photocopies of readable ID go with the returned request and voted ballot, and a voter without them completes an alternative affidavit giving the last four digits of a social security number plus a drivers license or state ID number. Bill was referred to the Rules committee and not shown as passed.

findings.motion: Co-sponsor of HB 1231 No Voter Registration Changes At DMV (date shown is the bill's introduction date; date she was added not seen)
findings.note: Cairns is listed as a co-sponsor. The bill would stop voters from updating an existing registration (address, name, party change) at drivers license offices, requiring those changes at the county board of elections; the citizenship question at the DMV application stays in the text. Referred to Rules committee and not shown as passed.
